title: Catalog: a case can expect a refusal

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The request of the maintainer (relayed 2026-11-17, quoted in #2392): "have it setup a bunch of examples.. for debugging..". The body of #2392 specifies: "verify clean (no gouge, no refusal unless the case is about a refusal)".

## What

Let a catalog case expect a refusal. `case.toml` gets `expect = "post"` (default) or `expect = "refusal"`. A refusal case has no `.nc` file. It has a file `refusal.txt` with the exact refusal lines.

- The script does not catch the refusal. The script run ends with an error.
- The script saves the project before the refused step.
- The two tests in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` compare the recorded refusal lines with `refusal.txt`, byte for byte.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check` accepts a refusal case that has no `.nc` file.

If the `case.toml` sub-issue of #2392 is not merged, this issue adds the `expect` key itself.

## Evidence

- `every_catalog_case_opens_regenerates_verifies_and_posts_byte_for_byte` asserts `OpStatus::Ok`, an empty verification report and a successful post.
- `every_catalog_case_rebuilds_from_camscript` asserts exit 0 and a written `.nc` file.
- The script host records each refusal in the `errors` list of the run, also when the script catches it (`crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`). This law does not change.

This work is under the safety floor: it changes how a test reads a blocked post.

Done means: one refusal case passes. A changed refusal text makes the test red. A refusal case that posts makes the test red. The script host law does not change.

Part of #2392
